syllabusTopics: Logic and set: statements, logical connectives, truth tables, theorems based on set operations
Real numbers: geometric representation of real numbers, interval, absolute value
Function: domain and range of a function, inverse function, composite function; algebraic (linear, quadratic and cubic) and transcendental (trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic) functions

Curve sketching: odd and even functions, periodicity, symmetry (about origin, X- and Y-axis), monotonicity; graphs of quadratic, cubic and rational functions, trigonometric (asinbx and acosbx), exponential (e^x), logarithmic (lnx)

Matrices and determinants: transpose of a matrix and its properties; minors and cofactors, adjoint, inverse matrix, determinant, properties of determinants (without proof)
Quadratic equation: nature and roots of a quadratic equation, relation between roots and coefficient, formation of a quadratic equation, symmetric roots, one or both roots common
Complex number: imaginary unit, algebra of complex numbers, geometric representation, absolute (modulus) value and conjugate of complex numbers and their properties, square root of a complex number

card.title: Matrices and determinants: transpose, properties, inverse

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Matrices bring algebra to arrays. **Transpose** swaps rows and columns and obeys (Aᵀ)ᵀ = A, (A+B)ᵀ = Aᵀ+Bᵀ and the **reversal law (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ**; **multiplication** (AB)ᵢⱼ = Σₖ aᵢₖbₖⱼ is associative and distributive but **never commutative**, and AB = O tolerates non-zero factors.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: x (AB)^T = A^T B^T. x (AB)^T = B^T A^T (order reverses!).  ·  x Every matrix has an inverse. x Only square, non-singular matrices.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A skew-symmetric matrix can also be symmetric only in the trivial case A = 0, since A = A^T = -A^T forces every entry to be zero.  ·  Interchanging any two rows, or any two columns, of a matrix changes the sign of its determinant.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The determinant as a volume meter*** - |A| scales areas and volumes under x -> Ax; |A| = 0 collapses space, which is precisely why the inverse cannot exist.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: x AB = BA always. x Matrix multiplication is NOT commutative.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Find the transpose and the determinant of a 2x2 or 3x3 matrix, expanding a 3x3 determinant along the row or column with the most zeros.  ·  Find A^-1 for a 2x2 matrix by the adjoint method, then verify the result by multiplying A A^-1 to obtain the identity matrix.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 2x2 inverse: swap diagonal, negate off-diagonal, divide by |A|. |AB| = |A||B|. Solve AX = B: find |A|, adj A, multiply. Transpose and inverse: reverse the order.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2023 (verified PYQ): If A = [[2, 1], [3, 4]], find det(A) and A⁻¹. (3m)** — **Determinant:** |A| = (2)(4) − (1)(3) = 8 − 3 = **5 ≠ 0** ⟹ A is non-singular and invertible. **Cofactors:** C₁₁ = +4, C₁₂ = −3, C₂₁ = −1, C₂₂ = +2 ⟹ cofactor matrix [[4, −3], [−1, 2]]; **adj A = its transpose = [[4, −1], [−3, 2]]**.…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Verify the reversal law (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ for A = [[1, 2], [0, 1]] and B = [[1, 0], [3, 1]].** — **Left side:** AB = [[1·1 + 2·3, 1·0 + 2·1], [0·1 + 1·3, 0·0 + 1·1]] = [[7, 2], [3, 1]]; its transpose: **(AB)ᵀ = [[7, 3], [2, 1]]**.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Always verify A A^-1 = I after computing an inverse - the check is quick and catches transpose/cofactor slips.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Reversal laws share one reason: undoing "A then B" means undoing B first - transpose and inverse both read right to left.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Matrix: rectangular array, order m x n; addition entrywise for equal orders. Transpose theorems: (A^T)^T = A; (A + B)^T = A^T + B^T; (AB)^T = B^T A^T (reversal); (kA)^T = kA^T. Multiplication: (AB)_ij = sum_k a_ik b_kj, needs cols(A) = rows(B); associative, distributive, NOT commutative; AB = O does not force A = O or…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Computer graphics composes transforms as matrix products - and un-composes them in reverse order, the reversal law on screen.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): Solve the system x + y = 5, 2x − y = 1 by the matrix (inverse) method.** — **Matrix form:** A = [[1, 1], [2, −1]], X = [x, y]ᵀ, B = [5, 1]ᵀ, so **AX = B**. **Determinant:** |A| = (1)(−1) − (1)(2) = −3 ≠ 0 ⟹ unique solution exists.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Rectangular Arrays With Algebra A **matrix** is a rectangular array; its algebra (transpose, sums, products) and the determinant machinery turn linear systems into single computations. The theorems: transpose laws, matrix multiplication's non-commutativity, invertibility via |A| ≠ 0, and **A⁻¹ = adj A/|A|**.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Matrix basics and algebra - Order m × n; equality needs equal orders and matching entries. **Addition** entrywise (same orders only); **scalar multiplication** distributes. - **Transpose:** Aᵀ swaps rows and columns. **Theorems:** (Aᵀ)ᵀ = A; **(A + B)ᵀ = Aᵀ + Bᵀ**; **(AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ** (reversal law); (kA)ᵀ = kAᵀ.…  ·  ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Transpose** | Rows ↔ columns | (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ | | **Non-singular** | |A| ≠ 0 — invertible | rotation matrices | | **Adjoint** | Transpose of the cofactor matrix | adj A feeds A⁻¹ | | **Singular** | |A| = 0 — no inverse | projection matrices |

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Multiplying one whole row of an n x n matrix by k multiplies its determinant by k, not by k^n.  ·  The determinant of an odd-order skew-symmetric matrix is zero, even though the matrix itself need not be zero.  ·  If |A| = 5 for a 3x3 matrix then |adj A| = 5^2 = 25, not 5, because the exponent is n - 1.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Verified PYQ: NEB 2023 (det and inverse of [[2,1],[3,4]]) - assigned to this row. Other items are NEB-style practice.  ·  "A is invertible iff |A| != 0; A^-1 = adj A/|A|; (AB)^-1 = B^-1 A^-1; (AB)^T = B^T A^T."  ·  Find det(A) and A⁻¹ for A = [[2, 1], [3, 4]].

rows.text: Classify a given matrix as square, diagonal, identity, zero, symmetric or skew-symmetric, and confirm that a skew-symmetric matrix has a zero diagonal.  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why multiplication reverses order - (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ and (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹ both reflect the same fact: to undo "apply A then B" you must undo B first, then A — socks before shoes, shoes off before socks.…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **Scalar vs matrix algebra** | Law | Scalars | Matrices | |---|---|---| | commutative product | yes | **no** | | AB = 0 ⟹ A = 0 or B = 0 | yes | **no** | | (AB)⁻¹ | 1/(ab) = (1/a)(1/b) | B⁻¹A⁻¹ (order reverses) | | cancellation | yes | only if invertible |

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 6. Common Confusions **Multiplication order:** AB needs cols(A) = rows(B); reversing kills the definition, not just the value.  ·  **(AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹, not A⁻¹B⁻¹:** the reversal law — the transpose version (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ is its twin.  ·  **adj A is the transpose of cofactors:** forgetting the transpose is the classic inverse-computation error.
